 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green and Graham Ike will start Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski is available after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers due to a lower-back injury. His return means that De’Anthony Melton will come off the bench. Ike gets his first NBA start, letting Green play his usual power forward role. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandin Podziemski (back) is probable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski is trending in the right direction after he was initially listed as questionable with a back ailment. He missed Wednesday’s loss against the Lakers with the same injury. Now that he’s been upgraded to probable, Podziemski, who appeared in all 82 games last season, should start alongside Stephen Curry against the Grizzlies Friday.

 Brandin Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, leading to De’Anthony Melton taking the starting spot. Melton played 21 minutes, while reserves Will Richard and Brandon Williams played 20 and 18 minutes, respectively. Expect a similar rotation if Podziemski can’t play on Friday.

 Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said on Wednesday that he’s hopeful Brandin Podziemski (back) will return for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 After missing practice on Monday, Podziemski will miss Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers due to lower back soreness. However, he may not be out long, with Kerr hoping Podz can play on Friday. De’Anthony Melton is the player whose role may expand the most while Podziemski sits.

 Podz missed practice on Monday and will now be unavailable for the season opener. There are high expectations for the type of impact he’ll make this season, so they’ll certainly miss him. De’Anthony Melton will likely replace him in the starting unit.

 Brandin Podziemski (back) did not participate in Monday’s practice. 
 This has been a bad 24 hours for the Warriors, who saw Stephen Curry suffer an ankle injury during Sunday’s open practice. Podziemski is dealing with a sore lower back, casting some doubt on his availability for Wednesday’s season opener against the Lakers. If he can’t play, De’Anthony Melton takes on added importance within the Warriors’ rotation.

 #2 
 Brandin Podziemski contributed 17 points (6-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Lakers on Tuesday. 
 Podz signed a five-year extension with the Warriors just a few days ago, showing how important he is to their future. He has been solid so far during the preseason and should be an important piece for the Warriors once again this season. Following a rough start to last season, Podz closed the year out well and will look to carry some of that momentum into this season. 
 Brandin Podziemski 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Brandin Podziemski has agreed to a five-year, $110 million extension with the Warriors, reports ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 The extension is fully guaranteed and includes a mutual option in the fifth year as well as a trade kicker, according to Charania. Podziemski is coming off his best season in the NBA where he played in all 82 games and set career-highs nearly across the board. He’s coming off the board in the ninth-round of fantasy drafts this year. 
 De'Anthony Melton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #8 
 De’Anthony Melton (thumbs) told NBC Sports Bay Area that he expects to play both games of back-to-backs this season. 
 Focusing on honing one’s craft during the offseason, rather than rehabbing from an injury, can make a significant difference for a player. That was the case for Melton this offseason, despite procedures on both thumbs. Last summer was spent recovering from a torn ACL, while a back injury was the issue in the summer of 2024. A healthy Melton can be a factor in fantasy basketball, especially category leagues, whether he starts or comes off the bench. His injury history puts him in “late-round flier” territory in drafts, but Melton can still be a steal for managers. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Brandon Williams has agreed to a one-year, $2.6 million deal to join the Golden State Warriors. 
 In his third season with Dallas, Williams enjoyed the most productive campaign of his career behind averages of 13 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.2 “stocks.” He’ll offer depth to a Warriors team that surprisingly stood pat during free agency, and Williams will compete for backup guard minutes with the likes of De’Anthony Melton and Will Richard.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 36 points (15-of-26 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Pistons. 
 Antetokounmpo has now had at least 35 points in each of his first two games in a Heat uniform. He played a more complete game across the stat sheet compare to the opener with 12 rebounds, five assists and three stocks. Still, the Heat lost to the Pistons by 17 after dropping the opener to the Timberwolves by 25. Miami will look for its first win of the season and probably get it against the reeling Hornets in Charlotte on Saturday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters there’s no injury update on Ausar Thompson (ankle) and Jalen Duren (thigh). 
 Thompson appeared to roll his ankle while Duren grabbed his leg and headed to the locker room midway through the second quarter. While there was no update from Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff after the game, the team said Duren was questionable to return with a thigh injury. It’s unclear if either player will be available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers, though more information about Thompson and Duren’s status should be available Saturday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Duncan Robinson had 17 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, two assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Heat. 
 Robinson is yet to make a two-point field goal so far this season, but he’s 10-of-19 from behind the three-point line in the first two games this year. The 32-year-old forward’s fantasy utility is mostly limited to his three-point shooting, but it looks like the right time to continue to ride the hot hand. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 John Collins had 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers against the Heat on Friday. 
 Collins had a quiet debut with six points in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, but he was excellent in the win over the Heat on Friday. The 29-year-old power forward was 9-of-15 from the field, including 5-of-6 from behind the three-point line. Jalen Duren (thigh) left with an injury in the second quarter and didn’t return, which likely led to more opportunities for Collins. With Duren’s status still up in the air, Collins could be in line for more usage again on Sunday against the 76ers. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Cade Cunningham had 16 points (5-of-8 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers in the Pistons’ 128-111 victory over the Heat on Friday. 
 Cunningham had another fine game as he filled the stat sheet and led the Pistons to another win to start the season. However, after turning the ball over five times in the win over the Celtics on Tuesday, he had seven turnovers against the Heat on Friday. Even opposing coaches like the Heat’s Erik Spolstra have pointed out that Cunningham isn’t necessarily a bad ball-handler, but commits a lot of turnovers thanks to almost always having the ball in his hands. That doesn’t offer much comfort to fantasy managers with Cunningham in nine-category leagues as he’s likely to be towards the top of the league in turnovers this year. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Brandon Miller had six points (2-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Hawks on Friday. 
 There’s no sugarcoating it; Miller is off to a rough start to begin the season. The 23-year-old small forward had 18 points in the opener, but shot just 7-of-21 from the floor. He followed that performance up by going 2-of-14, including 1-of-11 from behind the three-point line. He’s now 4-of-25 (16 percent) from behind the arc to begin the season. Miller was an almost incomprehensible -37 in 22 minutes in the 128-81 loss to the Haws Friday. Is this rock bottom? Because it feels like it can only get better from here. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Naz Reid had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Reid had seven turnovers despite only playing 24 minutes and that’s a crusher in nine-category leagues. Otherwise, he’s scored 37 points on 15-of-34 attempts with seven three-pointers in his first two games with the Hornets. That’ll play. If Reid can keep the turnovers under control, he’s well on his way to paying off his mid-round draft price.

 Miles McBride produced 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 McBride rebounded nicely from his poor showing in Tuesday’s loss to the 76ers, a game in which he scored three points on 1-of-5 shooting. Against the Celtics, Deuce shot 6-of-8 from three and scored 20 of the Knicks’ 32 bench points. The reserve role doesn’t help McBride deliver consistent fantasy value, but he can be an effective source of points and three-pointers in deep leagues.

 Jalen Brunson accumulated 19 points (7-of-17 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Brunson’s gotten off to a slow start by his standards, shooting 13-of-32 from the field in New York’s first two games. The Knicks star also didn’t shoot well from the foul line, missing three of his six attempts in Boston. Those rostering Brunson don’t have much to worry about, as the season is only two games old. However, they would certainly like to see him clean up his shooting in Sunday’s game against the Magic.

 Jalen Johnson had 19 points (9-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, three steals and one block in Friday’s game against the Hornets. 
 With less than two minutes left in the first half, Dyson Daniel hit the floor for one of his seven steals, leading to a Jalen Johnson alley-oop dunk on the other end. That pretty much encapsulates how the night went for the Hawks as Johnson led the team in scoring with 19 in the 128-81 blowout win. Johnson showed he was able to move past the extracurriculars with the Magic on Wednesday with his usual excellent performance against the Hornets.
